sections.content: constraint (e.g., medical, legal), Max-Reliables +0.062 floor improvement over balanced (0.812 vs. 0.750) may justify the latency cost. For all other deployments, balanced provides stronger joint qualityresponse-time trade-off. J.3 CROSS-PROFILE INTERACTION ANALYSIS The per-profile analyses above identify several recurring interaction patterns. We consolidate these into three principal interaction mechanisms, each grounded in the factorial ANOVA and DID probes. J.3.1 INTERACTION I1: EMBEDDING ENRICHMENT Evidence. strongest two-way interaction in the retrieval ANOVA. η2 = 0.102, = 4.48, < 0.001 on NDCG@10 (167 configs; Section 5). This is the Root cause. Enrichment methods (contextual retrieval, RAPTOR) prepend synthetic context to document chunks before embedding. The quality of the resulting embedding depends on how well the embedding model can encode this prepended context: High-capacity embedders (E5-large, BGE-M3, 1024d): The additional context provides useful signal, and the model has sufficient capacity to encode it. However, our results show that even with high-capacity embedders, enrichment does not improve over the none baseline (η2 enrichment = 0.144, best level: none). This suggests that on domain-focused corpora, the original document text already provides sufficient embedding signal. Low-capacity embedders (MiniLM-L6, 384d): The prepended context overwhelms the models limited representational capacity, diluting the embedding of the original text. This produces negative interaction: enrichment hurts more with weaker embedders. Implication for profile design. All SOTA profiles either use BGE-M3 (standard, balanced, MaxReliable) or MiniLM-L6 (speed), and none use enrichment. This is the correct design choice: the interaction analysis confirms that enrichment provides no benefit and may actively harm weaker embedders. Future work should evaluate whether enrichment becomes beneficial on open-domain corpora where document text alone may be insufficient. J.3. INTERACTION I2: EMBEDDING RERANKING Evidence. η2 = 0.110, = 2.92, < 0.01 on NDCG@10 (167 configs; Section 5). Root cause. Cross-encoder rerankers operate on (query, passage) pairs and produce calibrated relevance scores. Their effectiveness depends on the quality of the candidate set provided by the first-stage retriever: Strong first-stage retrieval (BGE-M3 + hybrid): The candidate set already contains mostly relevant passages; the reranker refines their ordering but has limited room for improvement. The marginal gain of reranking is moderate. Weak first-stage retrieval (MiniLM-L6, dense-only): The candidate set contains more noise; the reranker can rescue relevant passages from lower ranks, providing larger marginal gain. This produces compensatory interaction: reranking benefits weaker embedders more than stronger ones. The practical consequence is that practitioners with strong embeddings should invest less in reranking and more in other dimensions (compression, awareness). J.3.3 INTERACTION I3: QUERY AUGMENTATION AGENTIC GATE η2 = 0.191 (Type-III; raw η2 = 0.259), (12, 279) = 5.47, < 0.001 on faithfulness; Evidence. Holm-adjusted = 0.018 (122 configs; Section 5). This is the strongest interaction on faithfulness and near the pre-registered H1 threshold (η2 = 0.20). Root cause. Query augmentation (HyDE, RAG fusion) expands the retrieval input, producing richer but noisier candidate set. The agentic gate (CRAG, self-RAG, speculative RAG) filters this candidate set by evaluating each passages support for the generated answer:

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: Augmentation alone (no gating): Noisy candidates pass through to the generator, which may hallucinate from irrelevant passages. Faithfulness does not improve ( = 0.00 for RAG fusion; Section D.1). Gating alone (no augmentation): The gate filters standard candidate set, which may already be insufficient. Faithfulness improves modestly ( = +0.05 for agentic RAG). Augmentation + gating: The enriched candidate set provides the gate with more material to work with; the gate filters aggressively, leaving only high-confidence passages. The combined effect is superadditive: the gates precision increases because augmentation provides better recall. This is the only positive (superadditive) interaction we observe; all other significant interactions are subadditive (composition penalty). It operates across the retrievalgeneration boundary, confirming that the composition problem manifests asymmetrically: within-stage interactions are typically subadditive (overlapping function), while cross-stage interactions can be synergistic (complementary function). Worked Example: Augmentation + Gating Synergy on SciFact Claim (I3) Query (SciFact): Basophils counteract disease development in patients with systemic lupus. This claim-verification query requires retrieving passages that directly support or refute specific biomedical assertion. No augmentation, no gating HyDE augmentation + agentic gating Dense retrieval returns 5 passages about basophils and lupus, 2 relevant, 3 tangential (general immunology). Generator uses all 5 unfiltered. Produces answer citing one tangential passage one unsupported claim. Faithfulness: 0.75 HyDE generates hypothetical passage elaborating on basophil-mediated immune regulation retrieves 8 candidates including 4 relevant and 4 tangential. Agentic gate evaluates all 8: keeps only the 4 that directly discuss basophils in lupus contexts. Discards 4 tangential. Generator receives 4 high-relevance passages every claim grounded. Faithfulness: 1.0 Why this is superadditive: HyDE alone would add noisy candidates that reduce faithfulness (net = 0.00). Gating alone filters the original 5 passages but cannot improve recall beyond what dense retrieval provides ( = +0.05). Together, HyDE provides the richer candidate pool that the gate needs to select from, while the gate removes the noise that HyDE introduces, each component compensates for the others weakness. Implication for profile design. Max_reliable is the only SOTA profile that activates both query augmentation (via HyDE) and agentic gating, which explains its faithfulness advantage. However, the aggressive refinement paradox (G1) limits the practical benefit: the gate is too aggressive, discarding passages that would improve answer completeness. promising direction is to relax the refinement threshold (PARTIALLY_RELEVANT passes) while maintaining the hallucination check, which would preserve the I3 synergy without triggering G1. J.4 SCALING ROOT CAUSES The corpus scaling experiments (Section 5) reveal two phenomena that require mechanistic explanation: (1) log-linear degradation for retrieval-side profiles (SPEED, STANDARD) contrasted with effectively flat behavior for generation-oriented profiles (BALANCED, MAX-RELIABLE), and (2) rank crossover between STANDARD and BALANCED that is visible from 25K and statistically significant at 200K (p = 0.004). Log-linear degradation. As corpus size increases from 5K to 50K documents, distractor density in the candidate set increases proportionally. For fixed top-k retrieval, the probability that given candidate slot is occupied by distractor increases as 1 R/N , where is the number of relevant documents and is the corpus size. Since is fixed (the same queries target the same documents), the signal-to-noise ratio in the candidate set degrades logarithmically with . The degradation rate varies by profile because different features provide different levels of noise robustness:

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: Speed (0.115/decade, R2 = 0.90): No noise filtering; degradation rate matches the raw retrievers sensitivity to distractors. Standard (0.055/decade, R2 = 0.89): HyDE and reranking provide partial noise filtering, but the reranker sees the same degraded candidate set. Balanced (0.015/decade): Context compression and document awareness provide generationside noise filtering that is independent of candidate set quality; even when the retriever returns noisier candidates, compression distils the relevant spans. Max reliable: Not measured at 50K due to computational budget, but the agentic pipelines iterative refinement provides an additional noise filter. Rank crossover between STANDARD and BALANCED. The standard profiles advantage over balanced at 5K (+0.006 NDCG@10) reverses between 15K and 25K. The gap trends in the predicted direction at 50K100K but is not statistically significant through 100K (p > 0.17, Welchs t, = 3 seeds per cell); it firms at 200K ( = +0.059; = 0.004). The root cause is the asymmetric scaling of retrieval-side vs. generation-side defenses: Retrieval-side defenses (HyDE, reranking) operate on the candidate set, whose quality degrades with scale. HyDEs hypothetical documents are generated from the query, not the corpus, so they do not adapt to increasing distractor density. The reranker scores each candidate independently, so its effectiveness degrades linearly with the fraction of distractors in the candidate set. Generation-side defenses (compression, awareness) operate on the output of retrieval, after reranking has already selected the top-10. Even when these top-10 passages contain more noise at scale, compression can extract the relevant spans, and document awareness provides stable grounding that does not degrade with corpus size. Worked Example: Scale Crossover Mechanism at 50K Documents (C3) Query (HotpotQA): Cooperative Living Organization is located in city that is the county seat of. . . At 5K documents (base corpus): Standard: top-20 candidates contain 6 relevant passages (low distractor density). Reranker selects 4/ relevant. NDCG@10 = 0.71. Balanced: same retrieval quality (shared stack), but compression removes 50% of tokens some context lost. NDCG@10 = 0.69. Standard wins by +0.02: compression discards useful tokens when passages are already high-quality. At 50K documents (+45K distractors injected): Standard: top-20 now contains 12 distractors about other cooperatives and other county seats (near-miss semantic matches). Reranker promotes 3/5 relevant, but 2/5 are distractors it cannot distinguish. Generator sees 2 irrelevant full-length passages (1,600 tokens of noise). NDCG@10 = 0.44. Balanced: same degraded top-20, same 2/5 distractors in the reranked set. But: (a) extractive compression removes the irrelevant spans from the 2 distractor passages, retaining only sentences mentioning county seat; (b) 100-token document prefix tells the generator which documents are about cooperatives vs. county government. NDCG@10 = 0.48. Balanced wins by +0.04: compression and awareness filter noise that the reranker cannot. The crossover mechanism: at small scale, the reranker alone provides sufficient noise filtering and compression adds unnecessary information loss. At large scale, the rerankers candidate set degrades (fixed top-20 from larger, noisier pool), and generation-side defenses become the binding constraint. This analysis provides causal support for the H3 hypothesis premise: profile rankings are not scaleinvariant because different features have different scaling slopes. profile optimized for small-scale retrieval (standard) will be overtaken by profile with better generation-side defenses (balanced) as scale increases. J.5 SUMMARY OF ROOT CAUSES BY MECHANISM Table 68 consolidates the root cause analysis across all four SOTA profiles, mapping each mechanism to the profiles it affects and its measured impact. Design principles emerging from the analysis. Three actionable principles emerge from this root cause analysis:

sections.title: K RAG METHODS CATALOG
sections.content: This appendix catalogs the techniques associated with the eight component dimensions varied in the factorial experiment. These dimensions sit within the nine-stage workflow described in Section 3: document processing and the base answer generator were held fixed, while D8 varies agentic control around generation. Practitioners seeking implementation details for any method can refer to the cited papers; our implementations follow the original algorithms unless noted. K.1 EMBEDDING MODELS (D1) all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim) lightweight sentence-transformer distilled from MiniLM (Wang et al., 2020) via knowledge distillation on 1B sentence pairs. Fast inference (10K sentences/s on GPU) at the cost of lower representation capacity. Used in the SPEED profile. BAAI/bge-m3 (1024-dim) unified embedding model supporting dense, sparse (lexical weights), and ColBERT-style multi-vector retrieval (Chen et al., 2024a). Trained on multilingual data with 8K context window. Our default embedding for all non-speed profiles. intfloat/e5-large-v2 (1024-dim) text embedding model trained with contrastive learning on large-scale text pairs, achieving strong performance on the MTEB benchmark (Wang et al., 2022). BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 (1024-dim) An English-focused embedding model from the BGE family (Xiao et al., 2024), optimized for retrieval via retromae pre-training and contrastive fine-tuning.

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: K.2 CHUNKING STRATEGIES (D2) Fixed-size chunking Splits documents into fixed-length segments (512 tokens in our experiments) with configurable overlap. Simple and deterministic. Semantic chunking Groups consecutive sentences whose embeddings are within similarity threshold, producing semantically coherent chunks (Chen et al., 2024b). Chunk boundaries align with topic shifts. Sentence-window chunking Each chunk centers on single sentence but includes configurable window of surrounding sentences as context. Preserves local coherence while maintaining fine-grained retrieval units. Hierarchical chunking Creates parent chunks (2000 tokens) containing child chunks (400 tokens). Retrieval operates on children; auto-merge promotes to parents when multiple children from the same parent are retrieved, recovering broader context (Sarthi et al., 2024). Structure-aware chunking Splits documents along structural boundaries extracted during document parsing (headings, sections, tables, code blocks) rather than by fixed token counts. Preserves layout semantics from the source format (Markdown, HTML, PDF) and keeps related structural units, table rows, list items, code blocks, in single chunk; parsed via Docling (Auer et al., 2024). Recursive chunking Splits documents hierarchically using prioritized list of separators (paragraph sentence clause token), recursively subdividing any segment that exceeds the target chunk size. Produces variable-length chunks that respect natural text boundaries while bounding chunk size, pattern popularized by LangChain and LlamaIndex as the default general-purpose splitter. K.3 INDEX-TIME ENRICHMENT (D3) None Chunks are indexed as-is without additional processing. Contextual retrieval Prepends brief document-level summary (generated by an LLM) to each chunk before embedding, improving retrieval precision without changing the retrieval model (Anthropic, 2024). RAPTOR Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval. Clusters chunks and generates recursive summaries at multiple levels of abstraction, enabling retrieval at varying granularity (Sarthi et al., 2024). GraphRAG Extracts entities and relationships from documents to build knowledge graph. Graph traversal augments vector search with structured reasoning over entity connections (Edge et al., 2024). Excluded from the factorial experiment due to entity-extraction cost (14h per ingestion combo). K.4 RETRIEVAL MODES (D4) Dense-only Approximate nearest-neighbor search over embedding vectors using cosine similarity. BM25 (sparse lexical) The classical Okapi BM25 ranking function (Robertson & Zaragoza, 2009), term-frequency / inverse-document-frequency score with length normalization and saturation parameters. Serves as the sparse baseline in our executable comparisons  (Table 60)  and as the lexical component of all hybrid retrieval modes below. SPLADE (learned sparse) learned sparse expansion model (Formal et al., 2021; 2022) that produces weighted term vectors by expanding queries and documents over BERT vocabulary, enabling lexical match on semantically related terms.

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: Hybrid-BM25 Combines dense retrieval with BM25 lexical matching (Robertson & Zaragoza, 2009) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) (Cormack et al., 2009). The fusion weight α controls the densesparse balance. Hybrid-SPLADE Replaces BM25 with SPLADE (Formal et al., 2021), combined with dense retrieval via RRF. Hybrid (RRF fusion) Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack et al., 2009; Bruch et al., 2023) is the rank-aggregation algorithm that underlies all LASAGNA hybrid modes: each result list contributes score 1/(k + ri) for document at rank ri (we use the standard = 60), and the fused ranking sorts by summed score. Robust to per-retriever score scales and the default fusion for combining dense and sparse signals. Graph-based retrieval Augments vector retrieval with traversal over knowledge graph extracted at index time. For query, entities and neighbors within hops are materialized as additional passages alongside the top-k vector hits, broadening recall on multi-hop questions (Edge et al., 2024). Shares the ingestion pipeline with the GraphRAG enrichment (Section K.3) and was excluded from the factorial on cost grounds (Section A.4). Structured-RAG comparators (extension). parallel line of work replaces flat vector retrieval with graphor schema-based indexes: HippoRAG (Gutiérrez et al., 2024) runs personalized PageRank over an entity graph, KAG (Liang et al., 2024) fuses schema-aware knowledge-graph traversal with semantic layer, and hierarchical extensions such as TreeRAG (Tao et al., 2025) add document-tree structure. These systems are complementary to LASAGNA: each replaces the retrieval-stage internals while preserving the stage-isolation interface, so they can be dropped in as an additional D4 (retrieval) level and evaluated under the same factorial protocol. We did not include them in the 242-cell design because the D-optimal set was locked at pre-registration; natural extension is to test whether graph-based indexing changes the D5D8 composition patterns reported in Table 42. K.5 QUERY AUGMENTATION (D5) None The original query is used as-is for retrieval. HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) An LLM generates hypothetical answer documents; their embeddings are averaged with the query embedding to improve recall for underspecified queries (Gao et al., 2023a). RAG-Fusion Generates multiple query variants via an LLM, retrieves for each, and merges results via RRF (Rackauckas, 2024). Broadens the retrieval scope at the cost of additional LLM calls. Query decomposition Decomposes complex queries into sub-questions, retrieves for each, and aggregates evidence. Effective for multi-hop reasoning (Press et al., 2023). Step-back prompting Generates more abstract step-back question that captures the high-level intent, retrieves for both the original and abstracted queries (Zheng et al., 2024). K.6 RERANKING (D6) None Retrieved passages are returned in their original retrieval order. Single cross-encoder (CE) cross-encoder model (mxbai-rerank-large-v1 in our experiments) scores each querypassage pair jointly, reranking the top-k results (Nogueira & Cho, 2019). Ensemble reranking Combines scores from multiple rerankers (cross-encoder + ColBERT-style) via score fusion.

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) Iteratively selects passages that are both relevant and diverse, penalizing redundancy (Carbonell & Goldstein, 1998). Our experiments find this consistently hurts NDCG@10 in domain-focused corpora (Section 5). K.7 CONTEXT COMPRESSION (D7) None Full retrieved passages are passed to the generator. LLMLingua (extractive) Extractive compression that removes tokens with low information content according to small language model, reducing context length while preserving key information (Jiang et al., 2023a). K.8 AGENTIC QUALITY GATES (D8) None Single-pass generation without quality verification. CRAG (Corrective RAG) lightweight evaluator grades retrieval quality; if confidence is low, the system triggers web search or knowledge refinement (Yan et al., 2024). Self-RAG The generator emits reflection tokens that gate retrieval and self-assess generation quality, iteratively refining the answer through multi-turn retrieval and verification (Asai et al., 2024). Speculative RAG Generates multiple draft answers from different retrieved subsets and uses verifier to select the best, trading latency for answer diversity (Wang et al., 2025). Quality gates (hallucination filter) gate that sits between retrieval and generation and accepts chunk only if an LLM judge classifies it as supporting the question; chunks below the threshold are dropped. Shared machinery across CRAG, Self-RAG, and Speculative-RAG, and used directly in the MAX-RELIABLE profile (Section I.1.4). Raises the faithfulness floor but can starve the generator on multi-hop queries (Section J.2.4). Multi-hop refinement loop An iterative retrieverefinegenerate loop: after an initial retrieval and draft answer, the system issues follow-up retrievals based on what the draft is missing, repeats for up to iterations (3 in our experiments), and generates the final answer from the aggregated context. Related schemes include IRCoT (Trivedi et al., 2023) and FLARE (Jiang et al., 2023b); our implementation runs inside the same agentic graph as the quality-gate filter. TERMS, COMMON QUESTIONS, AND RELEASED RESOURCES This appendix gathers the papers terms in one place, answers the questions reader is likely to bring to it, each with pointer to the full account, and lists what is released. Keywords. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG); RAG evaluation; compositionality of RAG techniques; ablation study; factorial design; pre-registration; corpus scaling; reranking; hybrid retrieval; query augmentation; agentic RAG; answer faithfulness; NDCG@10; BEIR. L.1 TERMS LASAGNA. An open-source framework for evaluating new RAG components inside complete modern pipeline, with fixed interface per stage that the framework enforces, so new component drops into one stage and is measured against the same surrounding stack used by every reported configuration (Section 3). Dimension. One of the eight experimental factors of the study  (Table 10)  .

sections.content: Profile. One of the four operational RAG compositions distilled from the factorial and ablation sweeps as the best-observed configurations for distinct points on the retrieval-faithfulnesslatency envelope: SPEED, STANDARD, BALANCED and MAX-RELIABLE (Section I.1). Track. One of the two evaluation surfaces: retrieval or end-to-end (Section 4). NDCG@10. The retrieval-quality metric: whether the right documents are retrieved, following the BEIR convention (Thakur et al., 2021) (Section C.1). Answer faithfulness. Whether the generated answer is grounded in the retrieved context, scored with RAGAS (Es et al., 2024) (Section C.1). Composition shortfall. How far combined pipelines gain falls below the gain predicted by adding up its techniques measured one at time; 63% for the three strongest retrieval techniques (Section 5). Joint hypervolume (HV). NDCG@10 Faith max(0, 1 latency/Lref ) at Lref =30 s, the joint quality-latency envelope used to compare profiles (Zitzler et al., 2003)  (Table 2)  . L.2 COMMON QUESTIONS Do RAG improvements measured one component at time hold when the components are combined? Not reliably for retrieval. The three strongest single-component retrieval improvements predict +47% NDCG@10, and the pipeline containing all three realizes +17%, 63% shortfall. Across 17 tested combinations the shortfall ranges from 7% to 72%, with median of 41%. Faithfulness gains combine nearly as measured: +28% predicted, +32% realized (Sections D.14 and 5). Do retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same RAG design choices? No. In the factorial study, embedding, enrichment and reranking dominate the retrieval-quality metric (NDCG@10), whereas query augmentation and agentic gating dominate answer faithfulness, which measures whether generated claims are supported by the retrieved context. Optimizing RAG pipeline for one metric can hurt the other, so new components should be evaluated on both (Section 5). Does the best RAG pipeline on small corpus stay the best at large scale? Not necessarily. Across corpora from 5K to 200K documents, STANDARD leads at 5K and 15K, while BALANCED leads from 25K through 200K, where it exceeds STANDARD by 13.7% relative NDCG@10 (p = 0.003, three seeds). Rankings from small-corpus ablation studies should therefore be revalidated at the corpus scale deployment will use (Sections B.3 and 5). Is there one best RAG pipeline? No complete RAG profile is best on every metric. SPEED is fastest, STANDARD leads NDCG@10 and achieves the highest joint hypervolume (0.523 at 30 reference), and the agentic BALANCED and MAX-RELIABLE profiles lead faithfulness at higher response time. The best configuration depends on the target metrics, and adding components does not guarantee better pipeline (Section 5). How was the study designed? Three hypotheses were pre-declared before the experiments ran (van Miltenburg et al., 2021). The study tests 450 configurations across eight benchmarks: 167configuration D-optimal design (Fedorov et al., 1972) over the eight dimensions, 138 non-factorial ablation configurations across 24 targeted ablations, and corpus-scaling sweep from 5K to 200K documents. Deviations from the pre-registration are reported (Sections A.6 and 4). Which benchmarks, metrics and models does the paper use? Five BEIR retrieval sets (Thakur et al., 2021): NFCorpus (Boteva et al., 2016), FiQA (Maia et al., 2018), SciFact (Wadden et al., 2020), ArguAna (Wachsmuth et al., 2018) and HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018); and three question-answering sets: SQuAD v2 (Rajpurkar et al., 2018), HotpotQA and MuSiQue (Trivedi et al., 2022). Retrieval is scored with NDCG@10 and answers with RAGAS faithfulness (Es et al., 2024), judged by GPT-5.1. generator-substitution check replaces GPT-5.1 with Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Sections B.2, C.1 and F.9). Was the pre-declared interaction test (H1) met? No. It asked whether pairwise interactions explain at least 20% of the variance in faithfulness, and they do not. focused follow-up, prespecified before it ran, confirms that the interaction the broad analysis flagged is real (p = 0.007)

How should new RAG technique be evaluated? Inside representative complete pipeline, on both retrieval quality and answer faithfulness, and at the corpus scale it will be used at. Gains measured in isolation are not reliable predictors of realistic performance. LASAGNA supports this: component registered with one decorator is measured against the same surrounding stack as every reported configuration, with paired statistical test (Sections 3 and 6). What are the limitations? The evaluation uses one constructed English multi-domain test bed, at most 93 retrieval queries and 200 generation queries per experiment, in five focused domains. It does not test multilingual corpora, real enterprise or private data, open-weight generators, or crossorganizational large corpora. Faithfulness is measured under two generator models, sensitivity check rather than sweep, and absolute faithfulness scores rest on one judges calibration (Limitations, after Section 6). Where are the code and the project page? The LASAGNA code is at https://github. com/dolev31/lasagna, and the project page, with figures and summary of the results, is at https://dolev31.github.io/lasagna/. The pre-registration is archived at https://github. com/dolev31/Lasagna-Retrieval-Augmented-Generation-Compositionality. L.3 WHERE THIS WORK SITS The paper sits between RAG methods research (Lewis et al., 2020; Gao et al., 2023b), RAG evaluation frameworks and metrics (Es et al., 2024; Saad-Falcon et al., 2024; Yu et al., 2024), retrieval benchmarking (Thakur et al., 2021), toolkits that compose RAG pipelines (Jin et al., 2025; Rau et al., 2024) or search over them (Kim et al., 2024), and the design of experiments for comparing many configurations (Montgomery, 2021; Fedorov et al., 1972). Its contribution is measurement of how techniques compose, not new technique.
